issue.title: `@commit:` completion stops offering SDD sidecar commits
issue.description: `@commit:` completion — in the ACE prompt bar and in every LSP editor — offers only commits from repositories a human writes code in. SDD sidecar repositories (`plans`, `beads`, `agents`, `research`) contribute no completion rows, while a `@commit:<sidecar>@<sha>` reference typed in full still resolves at launch exactly as it does today.

issue.title: Repository kind on the wire, sidecars skipped in commit enumeration
issue.description: core_kind_filter: add a defaulted `kind` field to `ArtifactRefRepositoryWire` and skip `kind == "sidecar"` repositories in `append_commit_candidates` before spawning `git log`, leaving `resolve_commit` and every other kind untouched.

issue.title: The host labels each repository and proves both surfaces agree
issue.description: host_repo_kind: carry `RepoRecord.kind` into `ArtifactRefRepository` and its wire form in `artifact_ref_context()`, extend the prompt-bar/LSP parity test with a sidecar repository, assert sidecar resolution still succeeds, and correct the two documentation sentences that promise commits from every local checkout.

issue.title: Raise the published sase-core-rs floor
issue.description: core_floor: once the release carrying `core_kind_filter` is published, raise the `sase-core-rs` lower bound in `pyproject.toml` so an installed sase cannot silently run the unfiltered enumeration.

payload.entry: Implemented core repository kind wire field and sidecar commit-inventory filter in linked sase-core; verified cargo fmt --all --check and cargo test -p sase_core.

Carried RepoRecord.kind into ArtifactRefRepository/to_wire() and artifact_ref_context(); extended tests/artifact_refs/test_context.py to assert kind propagation; extended the prompt-bar/LSP parity test in tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_artifact_ref_completion_catalog.py with a kind=sidecar fixture holding the newest commit, verifying it is excluded from both surfaces, truncated_payloads is unaffected, and @commit:<sidecar>@<sha> still resolves via _resolve_for_launch (D4 invariant). Corrected the two local-git-checkout sentences in docs/editor.md and docs/getting_started.md to note sidecar exclusion and full-reference resolution. Verified with just check (fmt, lint, test) — all green.

Blocked: verified linked sase-core is tagged v0.17.14 with core_kind_filter, but PyPI still reports latest sase-core-rs as 0.17.13 and https://pypi.org/pypi/sase-core-rs/0.17.14/json returns 404, so the pyproject floor cannot be raised yet.

Acceptance cleanup added the named sidecar repository-kind constant and repository_is_sdd_sidecar predicate before checkout probing/git log, documented commit inventory as non-sidecar-only because SDD sidecars are machine-written stores, expanded the kind matrix to retain empty, primary, linked, and external repositories while excluding sidecar, and verified cargo fmt --all --check plus cargo test -p sase_core.

Raised the host dependency floor to sase-core-rs>=0.17.14,<0.18.0 and regenerated uv.lock to package version 0.17.14 from PyPI upload 2026-08-03T11:17Z. The approved starting-point focused run reproduced the pre-bump old-core sidecar completion failure; after just install, the focused artifact-ref/context and ACE completion-catalog tests passed 9/9, confirming sidecar completion rows are absent while explicit sidecar commit resolution still succeeds. Updated the telemetry smoke test expected minimum to 0.17.14. Full default just check ultimately passed; earlier default attempts only exposed the unrelated tracked flakes sase-e2 and sase-ct, both corroborated and passing in isolation.

Closed epic after verifying all children are done and the note audit found no PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP entries. Phase provenance: Rust core phase commit 3aa9d2a is contained in tag v0.17.14, and host phase commit 70410a05b carried RepoRecord.kind through prompt-bar/LSP context and explicit sidecar resolution coverage. Land cleanup fixed the reviewed Rust acceptance omissions by adding a named sidecar kind constant, repository_is_sdd_sidecar predicate, non-sidecar commit-inventory documentation, and an explicit empty/primary/linked/external-vs-sidecar test matrix; cargo fmt --all --check and cargo test -p sase_core passed. PyPI serves sase-core-rs 0.17.14 from the 2026-08-03T11:17Z upload, and pyproject.toml plus uv.lock now require/select 0.17.14. Focused post-bump tests passed 9/9, confirming sidecar completion rows are absent and explicit sidecar commit references still resolve; final default just check passed. The approved later-commit integration scan found no duplicate/conflicting host or Rust work, and unrelated flakes encountered during verification were corroborated on existing tasks sase-e2 and sase-ct.
